summary: Richard Jay Kohn worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1988, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata, was Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1994–2019), and was attested at the University of Chicago in 2021.

Richard Kieckhefer specializes in religious studies and history. He studied at Saint Louis University (~1964–1968) and the University of Texas at Austin (~1968–1972) before joining Northwestern University in 1975.

Richard King works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster, and under Daniel Mariau. He held posts at Stirling (~1994–2000), Vanderbilt (attested 2005–2009), and Glasgow (~2006–2011).
Richard M. Jaffe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1993–2000) and Duke University (~2000).
Richard Mahoney is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA under Paul Harrison at the University of Canterbury by 2002 and held a post there, attested in 2001.

Richard Morris was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Battersea Training College (~1852–1853), lectured at King's College School (~1869–1874), and served as headmaster of the Royal Masonic School for Boys in 1875.
Richard P. Boyle did graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under Joshu Sasaki. He taught at UCLA and held a post at the University of New Mexico (attested 2015).

Richard P. Hayes works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Toronto, studying under Bimal Krishna Matilal, Shoryu Katsura, and T. Venkatacharya. He held posts at Toronto, McGill, and New Mexico.
Richard Peter Hottelet, a scholar of Buddhist studies, studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, both attested in 1971.

Richard Pischel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau and under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Breslau, Kiel, Halle-Wittenberg, the Prussian Academy of Sciences, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908).
Richard Polenberg was an historian who studied at Columbia University (~1959–1964). He served on the faculty at Cornell University from around 1966 to 2011.

Richard Rorty was a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago (~1946–1952) and Yale (~1952–1956). He held posts at Wellesley (~1957–1961), Princeton (attested 1987), and Stanford (~1998–2007).

Richard Salomon specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He was a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1998–2017) and a visiting researcher at Soka University in 2007.
Richard Schmidt was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Mehliß and at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1887–1889).

Richard W. Lariviere studied Indology at Iowa (~1968–1972) and Pennsylvania (~1972–1976). He held posts at UT Austin (~1982–2006), Kansas (~2006–2009), and Oregon (~2009–2011), and was president of the Field Museum of Natural History (~2012–2020).
Richard Wilhelm was a Sinologist who studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium. He held posts at Peking University (~1922–1924) and Goethe University Frankfurt (~1924–1930).
Richard von Garbe was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied under Rudolf von Roth and Bhagavata Acharya, later succeeding von Roth to hold a chair at the University of Tübingen (1895–1927).
Richard von Glahn is a historian and Sinologist. He was appointed professor at UCLA around 1987 and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.
Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who conducted doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.
